title: My Daily Newsletter Digest — Monday, June 22, 2026
description: This episode covers the escalating standoff between Anthropic and the U.S. government over export controls on its top models, including a "Free Fable" letter from security researchers and tensions at the G7 AI summit. title: My Daily Newsletter Digest — Wednesday, June 24, 2026
description: Today's episode centers on AI entering the workplace, leading with Anthropic's Claude Tag, which embeds Claude into Slack as a delegatable "team member," and a Confidential Computing Summit push for data decentralization and agent security. description: OpenAI launches its first custom inference chip, Jalapeño, built with Broadcom, as the company pushes to own every layer of the AI stack. title: My Daily Newsletter Digest — Friday, June 26, 2026
description: This episode digs into the rise of AI agents and the guardrails forming around them, starting with OpenAI's new research showing agents like Codex overtaking chatbots in the workplace, followed by the $500 million bipartisan Raise Us initiative aimed at heading off AI-driven job disruption. It also covers a push to secure agents at the chip level from the Confidential Computing Summit, the Trump administration limiting the release of OpenAI's GPT-5.6, and Anthropic accusing Alibaba of a massive Claude data-harvesting attack. title: My Daily Newsletter Digest — Saturday, June 27, 2026
description: This episode focuses on the security risks of autonomous AI coding agents like Claude Code, explaining the "lethal trifecta" of internet access, broad permissions, and sensitive code that makes running them on personal laptops dangerous. Drawing on a special edition of The Deep View in partnership with Coder, it covers why IT teams block these tools, the irony that those who'd benefit most can't get access, and a proposed fix: moving agents to pre-hardened, centrally governed remote cloud environments. It closes with the bigger picture of running fleets of audited agents in parallel as a standard way of working.

Rounding it out are practical AI use cases, compute capacity squeezes, and quick hits on Codex, OpenAI hires, and new funding.

title: My Daily Newsletter Digest — Tuesday, June 30, 2026

description: Today's episode covers Anthropic's new efficiency-focused Sonnet five model and the return of its export-blocked Fable five and Mythos five models, plus Google's two new creative AI tools, Nano Banana two Lite and Gemini Omni Flash, amid backlash over its A24 film partnership. description: The lead story covers the US Commerce Department lifting export controls on Anthropic's frontier models Mythos and Fable five after a three-week standoff, plus OpenAI's parallel restriction on GPT five point six, and what these government-brokered safety terms mean as a possible new precedent for frontier AI launches. description: This episode explores the rise of "world models" in AI—systems that learn physics and spatial reasoning rather than just language—covering the massive early-stage funding flowing to labs like Fei-Fei Li's World Labs and Yann LeCun's AMI Labs, along with the compute and data challenges they face. Rounding it out are a review of Meta's smart glasses and quick headlines on Palantir, Microsoft, Kling AI, SpaceX, and Anthropic's chip ambitions.

description: This weekend edition explores how AI is reshaping corporate risk management, drawing on a piece from The Deep View and OneTrust that argues risk should be treated as an enabler of transformation rather than a barrier.
